flashcards.a: Singleton, Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Builder, Prototype.

flashcards.q: Why is Singleton usually a mistake as a class pattern?
flashcards.a: It hides global mutable state behind a private constructor + getInstance(), breaking test isolation, causing races under concurrent mutation, and structurally preventing 2 coexisting instances (e.g. multi-tenant). The need for one shared instance is real; fix via DI singleton scope or a cached provider, not the class pattern.

flashcards.q: What does @lru_cache(maxsize=1) on a provider function replace?
flashcards.a: The Singleton pattern — it caches and returns the same instance on every call, but the single-instance-ness lives in the composition/wiring layer, not baked into the class itself.

flashcards.q: What is Factory Method reduced to in Python and Go?
flashcards.a: A plain function plus a dict (Python) or a switch statement (Go) mapping a key to a constructor — no subclass hierarchy needed since both languages have first-class functions.

flashcards.q: What distinguishes Abstract Factory from Factory Method?
flashcards.a: Factory Method produces ONE product via subclass/parameter dispatch. Abstract Factory produces a FAMILY of 2+ related products that must stay mutually consistent (e.g. an S3 client must not pair with a GCS-family queue).

When there is only ONE product family (e.g. only Postgres, no MySQL). Building the interface for a family of one is speculative generality; collapse to a plain constructor until a second family is real.

flashcards.q: Why does Java need a fluent Builder class but Python usually doesn't?
flashcards.a: Java has no keyword arguments, so a constructor with many optional params becomes an unreadable/error-prone telescoping constructor, requiring staged .builder().x().y().build() calls. Python has keyword args + defaults, so a dataclass/Pydantic model with __post_init__ validation does the same job with no separate builder object.

flashcards.q: What is Go's equivalent of the Builder pattern, given it has neither keyword args nor classic inheritance?
flashcards.a: Functional options: variadic ...Option parameters where each Option is a function that mutates the struct being constructed, e.g. NewServer(addr, WithTimeout(5*time.Second), WithTLS(cfg)).

flashcards.q: What are the 4 problems with Java's Cloneable interface?
flashcards.a: 1) Object.clone() is protected. 2) It performs a shallow copy by default. 3) It can throw a checked CloneNotSupportedException even when every real implementation supports cloning. 4) It doesn't compose cleanly with generics or final fields. Most production Java uses a copy constructor or static copyOf() instead.

flashcards.q: What does copy.deepcopy handle correctly that a naive hand-written recursive copy would not?
flashcards.a: Cyclic references — deepcopy maintains an internal memo dict keyed by object id, so an object graph containing a cycle is copied without infinite recursion.

flashcards.q: State Peter Norvig's 1996 claim about GoF patterns in dynamic languages.
flashcards.a: In a language with first-class functions, closures, and multiple dispatch (Lisp/Dylan), roughly 16 of the 23 GoF patterns become invisible or trivial, because most GoF patterns exist to work around C++/Smalltalk's lack of those features.

flashcards.q: Give the one-line test for whether a codebase needs a named creational pattern class.
flashcards.a: Can this be solved with a function, a dict, and a validated dataclass? If yes, skip the pattern ceremony; reach for a named pattern only for genuine multi-backend family coherence (Abstract Factory) or multi-step validated construction (Builder).

flashcards.q: Why does a naive Singleton break a multi-tenant storage backend requirement?
flashcards.a: A Singleton structurally allows only one instance per process, but multi-tenant systems often need different, coexisting storage clients (S3 for tenant A, Azure for tenant B) resolved per request — incompatible with getInstance() by definition.

flashcards.q: Why is Prototype risky for objects holding live connections?
flashcards.a: Cloning copies the reference to the connection, not a fresh connection, so two logical objects end up sharing one socket — construction with side effects breaks the clone-instead-of-rebuild assumption.
